references.text: The Lord warns Moses that the people and the priests must not break through to see the Lord, or He will break out against them. This is the immediate context for verse 24.
Moses and Aaron, together with Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of Israel's elders, are called up to the Lord, but only Moses may come near the Lord. This shows the limited access to God's presence.
Aaron and his sons are chosen for priestly service. This is relevant because Aaron is specifically mentioned as the one who may go up with Moses.
Nadab and Abihu die when they offer strange fire before the Lord. This illustrates the consequences of approaching God in the wrong way, which the warning in Exodus 19:24 points to.
Korah's rebellion results in the earth swallowing them and fire consuming those who offered incense. This shows God's judgment on those who break through without permission.
The Lord strikes down the men of Beth-Shemesh because they looked into the ark of the Lord. This demonstrates God's holiness and the danger of approaching Him improperly.
Uzzah dies when he touches the ark of God. This illustrates the consequences of breaking through God's boundaries, as warned by 'pæn-jifrots bam' (so that He may not break out against them).

The author of Hebrews refers to the events at Sinai, including the fear and the warning that even an animal that touched the mountain had to be stoned. This is a direct New Testament reference to the context in Exodus 19.
Direct narrative continuation establishing the same theological principle regarding exclusive access to God's holy presence.
